## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("05_Mitochondria/01_build_mito_sets/a_script/01_build_mito_sets.qmd")
```

## Read MitoCarta and the protein map

MitoCarta 3.0 (downloaded 2026-09-28 from personal.broadinstitute.org/scalvo/MitoCarta3.0/) is the
inventory of human mitochondrial proteins and 149 curated MitoPathways. Genes are matched to the
representative protein per symbol, the rows `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` tests.

```{r read}
mitocarta <- here("05_Mitochondria", "00_Input", "Human.MitoCarta3.0.xls")
protein_map <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "protein_gene_map"
)
```

## Build the sets

The full list and each MitoPathway become one set; pathways nest, so a parent such as "Complex I"
holds its children's genes too.

```{r pathways}
# text columns stop readxl guessing types, which warns on this file
pathways <- read_excel(mitocarta, "C MitoPathways", col_types = "text") |>
  filter(!is.na(MitoPathway)) |>
  transmute(collection = "MitoPathways", set = MitoPathway, gene = Genes) |>
  separate_longer_delim(gene, ", ")
```

```{r membership}
all_mito <- tibble(
  collection = "MitoCarta", set = "MitoCarta",
  gene = read_excel(mitocarta, "A Human MitoCarta3.0", col_types = "text")$Symbol
)
membership <- bind_rows(all_mito, pathways) |>
  mutate(measured = gene %in% protein_map$gene[protein_map$selected])
```

## Check the complexes

The complex readouts downstream are "CI subunits" to "CV subunits", because the parent pathways also
hold assembly factors, which build a complex without tracking how much of it exists.

```{r complexes}
membership |>
  filter(set %in% c(paste(c("CI", "CII", "CIII", "CIV", "CV"), "subunits"), "Complex I")) |>
  summarise(listed = n(), measured = sum(measured), .by = set)
```

## Summary

Coverage per collection shows how much of MitoCarta the data can speak to.

```{r summary}
membership |>
  summarise(sets = n_distinct(set), rows = n(), measured_rows = sum(measured), .by = collection)
```

## Save results

`02_test_mito` and `03_complex_subunits` read `membership`.

```{r write}
write_xlsx(
  list(membership = membership),
  here("05_Mitochondria", "01_build_mito_sets", "c_data", "01_build_mito_sets.xlsx")
)
```
